recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. These products work—not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.

fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Yerasimos Stilianessis and Sophie Fletcher are a bio-dynamic duo with a huge amount of holistic health knowledge. Yerasimos is a transformational bodywork coach who incorporates the Human Design system into his approach, and Sophie is a PHD student in Depth Psychology with a strong grasp on the connection between emotional, mental, and physical health. These two brilliant beings combine knowledge of spirit and soma to form a powerhouse of health wisdom.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Medical Colonialism and Selective Outrage", "body": "Chance opens the members' hour by raising medical colonialism, a phrase he admits he had never heard before, as a way to look past the division being stoked at home toward vaccine and sterilization campaigns aimed at African nations. The guests answer that people tend to get outraged only over what they are told to, and argue that anyone truly concerned about child mortality there would fund clean drinking water and sanitation instead. Chance points listeners to the Corbett Report's four part series on Bill Gates, and the group recalls how large state-run eugenics programs were in the early twentieth century United States, including California."}, {"title": "Genes, Environment, and the Roots of Self-Sabotage", "body": "Chance asks whether we are slaves to our genes, and the answer is no: change your food, your thinking and your surroundings and inherited patterns can shift, because, as one line puts it, you can't heal in the same environment you got sick in. When Chance admits that \"just be real\" has never helped him stop self-sabotaging, Yerasimos starts with consumption. Stop watching commercials, he says, since the subconscious absorbs far more than we notice, then look hard at your crowd, using the image of crabs in a bucket pulling down whichever crab tries to climb out."}, {"title": "Individuation and Choosing What You Consume", "body": "Sophie brings in Jung's individuation process, the period of breaking from the comfortable and known to walk a solo journey, and ties it to her own choices. She stopped drinking in her twenties, weathered the peer pressure, and says she now has no noise around alcohol at all, adding that the couple held a deliberately dry wedding. She describes standing before a restaurant dessert display after three years without processed sugar and already feeling the fog it would bring. She still checks in with herself case by case rather than swearing anything off forever, and Chance recalls a reception bar his mother added anyway."}, {"title": "Addiction as Spirit Turned Inside Out", "body": "Chance frames addiction as the inverse of spirituality, quoting Jung's remark that alcohol is called spirits because the craving mirrors the soul's thirst for union with God, and noting that alchemists used alcohol to distill the essence from matter. He reads a Marion Woodman passage from Sophie's Instagram calling addiction our spiritual nature turned inside out. Yerasimos extends it to phones, overtraining and habit loops, urging listeners to jump off the hamster wheel by eating real food and changing their media and company, and argues that advertising to children should be illegal because young psyches cannot yet tell programming apart."}, {"title": "Creating Space to Choose, and Human Design", "body": "Sophie describes watching Joker specifically to spot the programming in the background, and credits Yerasimos with a favorite rule: never eat anything you have seen a commercial for. She explains mirror neurons through the lab monkey whose brain lit up as a scientist ate a banana. Yerasimos reads Viktor Frankl on the space between stimulus and response and says bodywork widens that space by breaking down armoring. He then outlines Human Design as a blend of the chakra system, the I Ching, the Kabbalah Tree of Life and astrology with neutrino science, while Sophie treats it as a self-awareness tool, not gospel."}]
